record.program_name: Riverside Local Affordable Housing Trust Fund (LAHTF), created by Council resolution March 12, 2024
record.administering_agency: City of Riverside Housing and Human Services Department
record.typical_award_size: Construction and permanent loans at simple interest of no more than 3% per annum, with repayments recycled into the fund. Seeded with a $1,500,000 transfer of PLHA funds; ongoing revenue from HOME, NSP, CalHome, PLHA and ARPA affordable housing program income (ARPA affordable housing allocation was $1,388,797) plus 50% of future sale proceeds of City-owned land bought with General Fund money. City applied for a $1,000,000 HCD Local Housing Trust Fund match (August 2024). Staff cite typical gap requests of $3M to $4M for 65 to 80 unit projects.
record.affordability_requirement: Low to moderate income households. Committee recommendations at creation: 99-year affordability term, priority for seniors and justice-involved people, and eligibility for market-rate developers that restrict 10% of rental units (or 5% of for-sale units). Loans funded with PIP Round 4 money require 55-year first-position covenants at or below 50% AMI.
record.next_deadline: No LAHTF NOFA issued as of 2026-11-08. The March 24, 2026 PIP Round 4 staff report says residual receipts from PIP loans will flow to the trust fund and staff will issue a NOFA once enough has accumulated. Contact Housing and Human Services (Agripina Neubauer, Housing Project Manager).
record.layering_notes: City-controlled gap layer that sits ahead of County HOME/PLHA (the County CDBG/HOME record covers the Urban County, which excludes the City of Riverside as its own entitlement grantee). Stacks with the City's own HOME, PLHA and PIP loans (separate records) and with 4% or 9% LIHTC. Capitalized mainly from recycled program income, so the balance is small relative to need; expect it to be combined with HOME and PLHA on the same project. If the LHTF state match was awarded it carries HCD LHTF regulatory terms. City pages on riversideca.gov are thin; staff reports were pulled through the Legistar web API (client riversideca).
record.prevailing_wage_basis: No LAHTF rule found; the March 12, 2024 staff report is silent on prevailing wage. City loans are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), but 1720(c)(5)(E) exempts privately owned residential projects whose public participation is below-market interest rate loans with at least 40% of units restricted for 20+ years at or below 80% AMI (applied in DIR PW 2016-035, Spring Park Senior Villa). Where a loan is drawn from HOME program income, HOME rules (24 CFR 92.354, Davis-Bacon at 12+ HOME-assisted units) follow that money. Outcome is project-specific.
record.audit_note: Leave unclear: only basis is the general Labor Code 1720(b) public funds definition; coverage turns on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. Searched LAHTF staff report, Labor Code 1720 and DIR coverage determinations 2026-11-08.

record.program_name: Housing Authority and Successor Agency land write-downs and surplus land dispositions (e.g., 2882 Mission Inn Avenue DDA, 11049 Bogart, 8733 Indiana)
record.administering_agency: Housing Authority of the City of Riverside; Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency of the City of Riverside
record.typical_award_size: Land conveyed at or near $1. Example: September 1, 2026 DDA conveys 2882 Mission Inn Ave (0.22 acre) to Grapevine Development for $1, a $245,861 write-down counted as HOME match, for 10 affordable units in a 64-unit mixed-use project; that project also pairs $900,000 City HOME and $250,000 City PLHA with LIHTC. Other Housing Authority sites: 11049 Bogart (DDA with NPHS, 22 PSH units), 8733 Indiana (RFP with adjacent Successor Agency parcel), 2348 University (duplex redevelopment).
record.affordability_requirement: Surplus Land Act: at least 25% lower income on the notice of availability, 55-year covenants; Grapevine DDA requires 2 units at 50% AMI and 8 at 60% AMI for 55 years.
record.next_deadline: Sites are offered through SLA notices and RFPs as they come up; watch Housing Authority agendas. The University Avenue Density Transfer Pilot (separate record) also targets City surplus parcels.
record.layering_notes: Land write-downs count as HOME match (City reports excess HOME match of $16.4M). Successor Agency parcels need Countywide Oversight Board approval and HCD SLA sign-off, which adds months. The County land program (county record) is separate.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. Below-market land transfers are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(3) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720). The Surplus Land Act sections read (Gov. Code 54233, https://california.public.law/codes/government_code_section_54233; 54233.5, https://california.public.law/codes/government_code_section_54233.5) impose affordability covenants only, not prevailing wage. No DDA or program term stating prevailing wage was found. The 2882 Mission Inn DDA also pairs $900,000 City HOME; HOME Davis-Bacon (24 CFR 92.354) applies only if 12 or more units are HOME-assisted, which the DDA staff report does not state.
record.audit_note: PW citation pass 2026-11-09: true was uncited and no program-specific rule was found; set unclear per Tier 3 rule (1720(b) alone does not support true).

record.program_name: City of Riverside HUD entitlement funds: HOME Infill Residential Development Program and CDBG (FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan)
record.administering_agency: City of Riverside Housing and Human Services Department
record.typical_award_size: FY 2026-27 HUD allocations total $9,050,906: CDBG $2,749,768, HOME $981,735 (of which $883,561 to the Infill Residential Development Program, plus about $200,000 HOME program income), ESG $250,428, HOPWA $5,068,975 (City is the HOPWA EMSA grantee for both Riverside and San Bernardino counties). Recent HOME loans: $1,508,234 Sunrise at Bogart (22 PSH units), $1,550,443 Mulberry Gardens Family (11 HOME units). HOME-ARP also used ($3,000,000 Mulberry Gardens Senior).
record.affordability_requirement: HOME: at or below 80% AMI with HOME rent limits; 20-year minimum HOME period for new construction, City typically records 55 years.
record.next_deadline: Public notice of funding availability released each December (last one December 2025) for the following July program year; FY 2027-28 notice expected about December 2026. Action Plan due to HUD by mid-August.
record.layering_notes: City is its own HUD entitlement and is outside the Riverside Urban County CDBG/HOME pool in the county record. HOME is small (under $1M a year), so it functions as a slice of the local gap. Federal Davis-Bacon applies at 12 or more HOME-assisted units. The draft Action Plan says the City dedicates its direct PLHA allocation to affordable housing development as additional leverage.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

record.program_name: City of Riverside Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) direct formula allocation, development loans
record.administering_agency: City of Riverside Housing and Human Services Department
record.typical_award_size: Five-year PLHA plan (adopted July 7, 2020) estimated $9,732,750. CY 2023 application $2,456,509 (March 2025). Development loans to date: $1,000,000 Golden Pierce (79 units), $1,053,907 The Aspire (32 youth PSH units), $380,562 Sunrise at Bogart (22 PSH units), $250,000 proposed for Grapevine (10 units). A large share also goes to homeless case management ($1,384,134 City Net).
record.affordability_requirement: PLHA rules: rental units at or below 60% AMI (up to 120% AMI for owner units), 55-year covenants.
record.next_deadline: Awarded through Council-approved loan agreements; uncommitted amounts may be transferred to the Local Affordable Housing Trust Fund ($1.5M already moved). Contact Housing and Human Services.
record.layering_notes: City receives its own PLHA formula share separate from the County PLHA record, so City projects can carry both a City and a County PLHA loan. Commonly stacked with City HOME and PIP on the same project (Sunrise at Bogart used PIP $1.44M, PLHA $380K and HOME $1.51M).
record.prevailing_wage_basis: HCD 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines contain no prevailing wage or Labor Code 1720 provision, and the City staff report is silent. PLHA loans are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), but the 1720(c)(5)(E) below-market loan exemption (40% of units at or below 80% AMI for 20+ years) can apply, as in DIR PW 2016-035. Outcome depends on project facts and other layered sources (City HOME triggers Davis-Bacon at 12+ HOME units under 24 CFR 92.354).
record.audit_note: Leave unclear: only basis is the general Labor Code 1720(b) public funds definition; coverage turns on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. PLHA guidelines and City staff report searched for prevailing wage 2026-11-08 with no hit.

record.program_name: Prohousing designation and Prohousing Incentive Program (PIP) loans, City of Riverside
record.administering_agency: City of Riverside Housing and Human Services Department (designation by HCD)
record.typical_award_size: City has received $2.44M in PIP to date: $1,000,000 loan to Mulberry Gardens Family (149 units) and $1,440,000 to Sunrise at Bogart (22 PSH units). Council authorized an application for up to $1,440,000 in PIP Round 4 (March 24, 2026); loans come back to Council project by project.
record.affordability_requirement: PIP-assisted units at or below 50% AMI; 55-year covenants in first position.
record.next_deadline: Prohousing designation (awarded March 30, 2023) expires January 1, 2027. The Housing and Homelessness Committee took up reapplication on August 31, 2026; a reapplication resolution and HCD submittal must happen before January 2027 for the City to keep PIP eligibility and Prohousing scoring points.
record.layering_notes: Designation also gives Riverside projects Prohousing points or preference in HCD competitive programs (AHSC, IIG and others), a meaningful edge for City sites. PIP residual receipts flow to the LAHTF. Risk: staff estimate 16 confident and up to 23 uncertain points against a 30-point threshold under the stricter 2024 criteria, so the designation could lapse. Recorded at city level because the City selects and lends to projects, although the money is HCD's.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: HCD PIP Round 4 Guidelines and the 2026 PIP Final Guidelines contain no prevailing wage provision (Labor Code is cited only for the H-2A agricultural employer restriction), and the City staff report is silent. PIP loans are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), but the 1720(c)(5)(E) below-market loan exemption can apply to 50% AMI covenanted projects, as in DIR PW 2016-035. Outcome is project-specific.
record.audit_note: Leave unclear: only basis is the general Labor Code 1720(b) public funds definition; coverage turns on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. PIP guidelines (Round 4 and 2026) and City staff report searched 2026-11-08.

record.program_name: Riverside density bonus, Municipal Code Chapter 19.545
record.administering_agency: City of Riverside Community and Economic Development Department, Planning Division
record.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Implements state density bonus law with a concession table (1 to 4 concessions; 100% affordable projects get 4 and, within half a mile of a major transit stop, up to three extra stories or 33 feet) and reduced parking ratios (1 space for 0-1 BR, 1.5 for 2-3 BR; 0.5 per unit near transit with at least 11% VLI or 20% low).
record.affordability_requirement: Eligibility per Gov. Code 65915: 5% VLI, 10% low, 10% moderate for-sale, 10% special populations, 20% lower income students, or 100% lower income with up to 20% moderate.
record.next_deadline: Applied through entitlement review. Zoning Code amendments (PR-2024-001746 and the 2025 omnibus PR-2025-001793) updated Chapter 19.545 for 2024 state law changes.
record.layering_notes: No local enhancements beyond state law found; the chapter tracks Gov. Code 65915. City has no inclusionary ordinance or in-lieu fee fund, and no adopted citywide affordable housing fee deferral program was found. Pairs with the University Avenue Density Transfer Pilot (separate record) on eligible sites.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

record.program_name: Moreno Valley density bonus program, Municipal Code Section 9.03.050 (with impact fee reductions)
record.administering_agency: City of Moreno Valley Community Development Department, Planning Division
record.typical_award_size: Implements state density bonus law plus a local fee incentive: 50% reduction of the development impact fee and parkland impact mitigation fee for VLI units and 25% for lower income units (Section 9.03.050.I.2). Up to four concessions; projects within half a mile of a major transit stop also get up to three more stories or 33 feet.
record.affordability_requirement: Gov. Code 65915 thresholds (5% VLI, 10% lower, 10% moderate for-sale, 100% lower income with up to 20% moderate, and special populations); 55-year affordability agreement for rental units.
record.next_deadline: Applied at entitlement; last amended by Ord. 1035 (December 16, 2025).
record.layering_notes: The fee reduction is a real local enhancement beyond state law and can be requested as an additional incentive. A City fee reduction may count as public funds under Labor Code 1720. No local housing trust fund, inclusionary ordinance or in-lieu fee fund was found for Moreno Valley. Code read on the zoneomics mirror.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific prevailing wage rule is recorded for this program. Section 9.03.050.I.2 reduces the development impact fee and parkland fee 50 percent for very low income units and 25 percent for lower income units; the density bonus itself provides no public funds (1720(a)(1)). Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720) counts fees paid, reduced, charged at less than fair market value, waived or forgiven by a political subdivision as public funds, so this relief can make a project paid for in part with public funds. Coverage then turns on project facts and 1720(c): (c)(1) private residential projects on private property not built under an agreement with a state agency, successor agency or housing authority, (c)(3) de minimis (subsidy under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost), and (c)(5)(E) where the public participation is below-market loans on a project with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI. Other public funds in the deal often decide the question.

record.program_name: Corona development impact fee waiver or deferral for affordable housing
record.administering_agency: City of Corona (City Council; Housing Services and Planning)
record.typical_award_size: Case by case. On the 2nd Street Family project the City deferred up to $2,000,000 in development impact fees into a promissory note repaid over 55 years.
record.affordability_requirement: Tied to the affordability terms of the project's DDA or density bonus agreement.
record.next_deadline: Requested at predevelopment and approved by Council resolution with the project agreement. The FY 2026-27 Action Plan commits staff to educate affordable developers on how to request a waiver or deferral.
record.layering_notes: No standing fee deferral ordinance was found; treat as negotiable. Deferred fees held as a City loan count as public funds for prevailing wage. Useful to reduce the gap at construction closing.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. Fees reduced, waived, deferred or reimbursed are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720); whether a project is covered depends on 1720(c)(3) de minimis (under $600,000 and 2% of project cost) and other 1720(c) exemptions. No program rule stating prevailing wage was found.

record.next_deadline: Negotiated through a development agreement; contact Community Development early in entitlement.
record.layering_notes: Housing Element programs commit the City to continue fee deferral and reimbursement and expedited review. Fee reimbursement is a public subsidy for prevailing wage purposes.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. Fees reduced, waived, deferred or reimbursed are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720); whether a project is covered depends on 1720(c)(3) de minimis (under $600,000 and 2% of project cost) and other 1720(c) exemptions. No program rule stating prevailing wage was found.
record.audit_note: PW citation pass 2026-11-09: true was uncited and no program-specific rule was found; set unclear per Tier 3 rule (1720(b) alone does not support true).

record.program_name: Palm Springs Affordable and Multi-Family Housing Incentive Program (Resolution No. 24654), impact fee reduction and deferral
record.administering_agency: City of Palm Springs (Planning and Building)
record.typical_award_size: Sliding scale reduction of developer fees and development impact fees from 100% to 1% based on the number and share of affordable units; deferral of fee payment to certificate of occupancy; 50% reduction for market-rate apartments; ADU fee reductions.
record.affordability_requirement: New housing restricted to lower income households for the affordable tier.
record.next_deadline: Rolling; no application deadline. Program adopted 2019 (Resolution No. 24654) and slated for continued implementation through 2021-2029 per the Housing Element.
record.layering_notes: Unusually generous for the Coachella Valley; stack with the City gap loans and the 93.23.17 density bonus. Fee reductions are public funds for prevailing wage. record.program_name: Palm Springs density bonus, Zoning Code Section 93.23.17
record.administering_agency: City of Palm Springs Planning Services Department
record.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Implements Gov. Code 65915-65918 with on-menu and off-menu incentives, parking alterations and waivers; the City Council may approve a density bonus above state limits by resolution with Housing Element findings.
record.layering_notes: The Council discretion to exceed state bonus limits is a local enhancement. No inclusionary ordinance or local housing trust fund was confirmed. Code read on the zoneomics mirror.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).
